title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. A is the Dieudonné ring W(k)[F,V] over a perfect field k of characteristic p. Its relations are F·λ = λ^σ·F, λ·V = V·λ^σ and FV = VF = p. The page writes π for σ acting on W_n. A_n = A/(F^n, V^n) is the two-sided quotient. Its finite modules are the Dieudonné modules of finite commutative p-group schemes killed by F^n and V^n, i.e. 'truncated' objects. On the previous page Grothendieck seeks a dualizing functor for A-modules of finite length, which is the algebraic counterpart of Cartier duality. He proposes two candidates. The first is D(M) = Hom_A(M, I), where I = lim_n A_n with transition maps multiplication by p, viewed as a bimodule. The second is D'(M) = Hom_{W_n}(M, W_n), with an A-structure given by twisted transposition.

This page, step by step:

1. Module structure on D'(M). For u ∈ Hom_{W_n}(M, W_n) he defines:
   - u·F = π^{-1}∘(u∘F),
   - u·V = π∘(u∘V),
   - u·λ = u∘λ.
   The twists by π^{±1} are exactly what makes u∘F, which is only σ-semilinear, back into a W_n-linear form. He checks the relation FV = p: (u·F)·V = π π^{-1}(u∘F∘V) = p·u, and likewise u·VF = p·u. So the dual of a left module is a right module. The involution s exchanging F and V converts it back to a left module.

2. The case M = A_n. A_n is a bimodule, so Hom_{W_n}((A_n)_g, W_n) (dual with respect to the left structure) carries two commuting actions.
   - The right action is as above.
   - The left action comes from right multiplication on A_n: F·u = u∘F_d, V·u = u∘V_d, λ·u = u∘λ_d.
   He warns that the two W_n-structures on this dual do not coincide. He then asks whether A_n ≅ Hom_{W_n}((A_n)_g, W_n) as bimodules. If so, I_n = A_n is the dualizing bimodule and D and D' agree.

3. Translation into a pairing. Such an isomorphism amounts to a biadditive pairing ⟨ , ⟩ : A_n × A_n → W_n.
   - Right A_n-linearity of the map amounts to: ⟨λx, y⟩ = λ⟨x, y⟩, ⟨x, yλ⟩ = ⟨λx, y⟩, ⟨x, yF⟩ = π^{-1}⟨Fx, y⟩, ⟨x, yV⟩ = π⟨Vx, y⟩.
   - Left linearity amounts to the associativity conditions ⟨x, λy⟩ = ⟨xλ, y⟩, ⟨x, Fy⟩ = ⟨xF, y⟩, ⟨x, Vy⟩ = ⟨xV, y⟩.
   - The associativity conditions mean ⟨x, y⟩ = ⟨1, xy⟩ = ⟨xy, 1⟩. So the pairing is ε(xy) for a single linear form ε : A_n → W_n.
   - The twisted conditions then mean that ε is a twisted trace, i.e. a Frobenius form with a Nakayama-type automorphism coming from σ.
   - The final box restates this as a W_n-bilinear map A_n ⊗_{A_n} A_n → W_n satisfying ⟨Fx, y⟩ = π⟨x, yF⟩ and ⟨x, yV⟩ = π⟨Vx, y⟩.

In short, the page tries to show that the truncated Dieudonné ring A_n is a (twisted) Frobenius algebra over W_n. That would make I = lim A_n an injective cogenerator realizing Dieudonné/Cartier duality as Hom into a bimodule. The ε is never written down; the verification is left open (the '?' over the isomorphism). The next page switches to Gauss–Manin connections, so the thread is dropped here.
errors: First block: 'u∘F = π^{-1}(u∘F)' should read u·F = π^{-1}(u∘F). Likewise 'u.V = π(u∘F)' should be π(u∘V); the D'(A_n) block writes it correctly as π(u∘V_g).
In the D'(A_n) block, 'Vu = u∘F_g' should be V·u = u∘V_d, a slip.

The previous page's note 'A_n est libre sur W_n' is false. The ideal contains F^n V^k = p^k F^{n-k}, so as a W-module A_n ≅ W_n·1 ⊕ ⊕_{i=1}^{n-1}(W_{n-i}F^i ⊕ W_{n-i}V^i). The note appears to be struck through. Freeness is in any case not needed, since W_n is self-injective and Hom_{W_n}(−, W_n) is a perfect duality on finite W_n-modules.

The naive candidate ε = 'constant term' is not symmetric: ε(F·λ·V) = pλ^σ while ε(λ·V·F) = pλ. Any working ε must be twisted. The page does not exhibit ε, so the claimed bimodule isomorphism is left unproved (it is marked with '?').

ideas.what: Dual of a module over the truncated Dieudonné ring via Hom_{W_n}(M, W_n), with F and V transposed and twisted by σ^{±1}
ideas.modern_name: Dieudonné-module description of Cartier duality, M ↦ Hom_W(M, W_n) or Hom_W(M, W[1/p]/W) with F and V swapped
ideas.where_published: Related material in Grothendieck's 1970 Montréal lectures 'Groupes de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974); exact form unsure

ideas.what: A_n = A/(F^n, V^n) is self-dual as a bimodule: A_n ≅ Hom_{W_n}(A_n, W_n), via a pairing ⟨x, y⟩ = ε(xy) with σ-twisted compatibilities
ideas.modern_name: Twisted Frobenius (quasi-Frobenius) algebra structure on truncated Dieudonné rings, with a Nakayama automorphism coming from σ
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (implicit in duality theory of finite Dieudonné modules)

ideas.what: Dualizing bimodule I = lim_n A_n (transitions given by p), with D(M) = Hom_A(M, I)
ideas.modern_name: Injective cogenerator / dualizing module for finite-length Dieudonné modules
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure; standard practice uses W[1/p]/W with transposed F and V

missed.claim: Grothendieck seeks to show that the truncated Dieudonné ring A_n is a (σ-twisted) Frobenius algebra over W_n. That would make Cartier duality an internal Hom into the bimodule I = lim A_n, rather than a Hom into W with transposed operators. He reduces the problem to finding a twisted trace ε with ⟨x, y⟩ = ε(xy), but does not finish.
missed.quote: A_n ≃? Hom_{W_n}((A_n)_g, W_n) isom de bimodules ... ⟨x,y⟩ = ⟨1,xy⟩ = ⟨xy,1⟩
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a ring-theoretic formulation of Dieudonné duality via the Frobenius-algebra property of A_n. It may be relevant to non-commutative or derived treatments of Dieudonné theory, such as Dieudonné complexes and the de Rham–Witt / Cartier–Dieudonné–Dwork setups. The result is likely easy and implicitly known, so its novelty is modest.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine but tidy exploratory computation: Cartier duality on finite Dieudonné modules recast as a self-duality of the truncated Dieudonné ring. The underlying duality is standard. The explicit twisted-Frobenius-algebra viewpoint is not prominent in the literature, but it is unfinished and probably folklore.
transcription_corrections: Line 2 of the right block: 'u∘F = π^{-1}(u∘F)' is written in the image as 'u.F = π^{-1}(u∘F)' (dot, as in the other lines).
'module dual [?] sur A_n' on line 1 is plausibly 'module à droite sur A_n' (the scrawl matches the later 'à droite').
In the D'(A_n) block, 'Vu = u∘F_g' appears as written in the image, but the intended reading is V·u = u∘V_d.
The note 'add.' near 'isom A_n → Hom' is likely 'à d.' (à droite), and 'assure [?] est [?] A_n-linéaire [?] à droite' likely reads 'assurent que c'est A_n-linéaire à droite'.
The 'attention' sentence likely reads: 'attention les deux structures de W_n-module sur I_n ne sont pas les mêmes'.
